gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-007 identifies missing factors in the product approximation estimate, whereas the gold issue concerns the omitted input norm in the operator-tail estimate for (I-P_N)F x. These are different formulas and failed operations.

ISSUE-017 challenges compactness, boundedness, and equicontinuity of mollified inputs for an L2 argument. It does not identify the distinct failure that H^s-continuity of F fails to provide continuity in the C supremum topology required by point-sampling approximation.

ISSUE-016 concerns uniform stability of F under mollification on an L2 ball. It does not recognize the separate domain-preservation obligation needed to make F[M_xi x] and F[x] defined for constrained operator domains.

ISSUE-017 explicitly recognizes that the claimed inclusion of mollified inputs in the same L2 ball does not follow from the norm inequality. Its presentation emphasizes the failed compactness/equicontinuity justification rather than the gold construction showing displacement of the center under mollification, but it diagnoses the full false localization concern.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The mollification argument does not establish that every mollified input remains in the local neighborhood B_r(x*) where the assumptions are invoked; an L2 norm contraction relative to zero is insufficient to establish localization relative to x*.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: The prediction uses the L2-boundedness/compactness manifestation rather than the explicit centered-at-x* calculation and nested-ball repair; no substantive gold concern remains unrecognised.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof fails to establish the claimed same-radius localization M_xi(B_r(x*)) subseteq B_r(x*) because the available norm inequality is relative to zero rather than x*.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that the claimed inclusion in B_r(x*) does not follow from ||x_xi||_{L2} <= ||x||_{L2}, directly recognizing failure of the localization obligation, though through a different supporting argument.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-016 critiques uniform mollification control on a fixed L2 ball. It does not identify the quantifier-order error requiring one network to work simultaneously for every center rather than allowing center-dependent neighborhoods and networks.
